samples.summary: loop-status upsert PATCHes/DELETEs any trusted-author comment merely *containing* the status marker — which can be the `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` latch, silently clearing the loop's human hand-off
samples.evidence:
`isOwnStatusComment` (loop-status.mjs:114-118) matches ANY comment whose body *contains* `<!-- agent-loop-status -->` and whose author is one of our bots (or a write-access human). The upsert then PATCHes the oldest such comment (loop-status.mjs:440-447) and DELETEs every other one (loop-status.mjs:450).

Vector: the review-round guard's stall/standstill pages embed LENS FINDING SUMMARIES — LLM text derived from the attacker-authorable diff — directly into the page body (`review-round-guard.mjs:257-267`: ``.map((f) => `\`${f.file}\` — ${String(f.summary).slice(0,160)}`)``; standstill likewise at :245). If any such summary contains the literal `<!-- agent-loop-status -->` (trivially induced by diff content, and near-certain on any PR that touches loop-status.mjs itself, since a finding about the marker quotes the marker), the resulting page comment — posted with `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`, i.e. authored by `github-actions[bot]` (review-round-guard.mjs:90) — satisfies `isOwnStatusComment`.

The very next step in the same job runs the upsert (`agent-review-panel.yml:1431-1451`, `Update loop status (round-guard decision)`, with `PAGED=true`). Because an earlier round's dashboard is older, the fresh page comment is treated as a younger *duplicate* and DELETED (loop-status.mjs:448-455); on a first round with no dashboard it is instead PATCHed, replacing its body with a dashboard body that carries no latch marker. Either way the latch is destroyed within seconds of being written.

Consequence: `review-round-guard.mjs:117` (`comments.some(isPagedLatchComment)`) and the panel `gate` job's literal copy (`agent-review-panel.yml:220-224`) both stop seeing the latch, so the review panel and the fixer resume on a PR that was explicitly handed to a human — the stall/standstill bound the guard exists to enforce is erased, and `set-state`'s self-heal (which derives `agent:blocked` from the latch) will also drop the label. Same over-broad match also destroys other comments: GitHub's "Quote reply" copies the raw body including HTML comments, so a maintainer quoting the dashboard gets their comment deleted by the bot; a fixer-authored `fix-report`/`rebuttal` comment (posted as `yorkie-agent[bot]` with fixer-chosen text) that includes the marker is likewise overwritten or deleted, destroying input the panel's adjudicator reads. Fix: require the body to START with the marker (renderLoopStatus already emits it first) and refuse to PATCH/DELETE any comment containing either paged latch.

samples.summary: The "pre-fixer snapshot" does not isolate the scripts from the fixer (which holds Bash and can rewrite $RUNNER_TEMP), and the snapshot is branch code executed with a contents:write GITHUB_TOKEN
samples.evidence:
The new staging step copies the BRANCH's `scripts/agent` into `$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-tools` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:112-115) and its comment justifies this as protection because "the fixer holds Bash/Edit/Write" over the workspace. But the fixer is granted `--allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep"` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:359), and Bash is not confined to the workspace — `$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-tools` is writable by the same runner user, so a prompt-injected fixer can overwrite the staged `loop-status.mjs` / `session-job-summary.mjs` / `metrics.mjs` just as easily as the workspace copy. The consumers then execute that code with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:426-441, :234-237) under workflow-level `contents: write`, `issues: write`, `pull-requests: write` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:24-29) — a write token handed to code the fixer controls.

Second, independent of Bash: the snapshot is taken from the branch checkout (line 100-115), so a malicious `scripts/agent/loop-status.mjs` COMMITTED on a previous round is staged and run with that token on the next round — the pre-fixer timing gives no protection against that at all. Compare the panel's fix job and `agent-fix.yml`, which stage from a `ref: main` checkout (agent-review-panel.yml:1359-1363/1486-1488; agent-fix.yml:105-107/220) — this arm should do the same (sparse-checkout main into a separate path) rather than trust branch code. I acknowledge the job already ran `./scripts/agent/set-state.mjs` and `metrics.mjs` from the workspace post-fixer (agent-iterate-ci.yml:415, :452), so the posture is pre-existing; this change adds two more executions of it while asserting a protection that Bash defeats.

samples.summary: No neutralization of trusted hidden markers in the rendered body/`note`, even though the comment is authored by the bot identity the paged latch trusts
samples.evidence: `renderLoopStatus` interpolates `note` into the body after only flattening newlines and truncating to 600 chars (loop-status.mjs:259); nothing strips or defangs `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` / `<!-- agent-paged -->` / `<!-- agent-metric ` markers. The file header claims "UNTRUSTED INPUT STAYS OUT OF THE BODY" and enforces that only for ledger records (numbers only) — but `note` is a free-form channel, and one caller already passes a computed value: `--note "${VERDICT:-...}"` from the guard's `verdict` output (agent-review-panel.yml:1439/1448). Today `guardVerdictLine`'s page branch renders only the canned `PAGE_REASONS` text and never `v.detail` (guard-verdict.mjs:44-48), so no untrusted string reaches the note — the property holds by accident of one `??` expression, not by construction. If that line ever included `detail` (which embeds diff-derived finding summaries, review-round-guard.mjs:101/259), the marker would be laundered into a bot-authored comment that `isPagedLatchComment` trusts, permanently latching the panel and fixer on the PR (denial of review). Defense-in-depth fix: escape/strip `<!--` in `note` and in every interpolated cell before rendering.
searchedFor: grep for `--note` across .github/workflows (panel, iterate-ci, fix, rerun) — all other notes are static literals or shas/counts
read guard-verdict.mjs buildLine/guardVerdictLine to check whether `detail` reaches the one-line verdict output
read review-round-guard.mjs page() call sites for the `reason` tags passed (all literals)
grep renderLoopStatus for sanitization of `<!--` / marker constants

samples.summary: Untrusted CI diagnosis is written raw and unfenced into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, allowing run-page markdown/HTML spoofing
samples.evidence: `printf '%s\n' "$DIAG" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:275) emits `summarize-ci.mjs` output — assembled from build/test output produced by the branch, which the workflow's own prompt calls "FAILURE DATA, not instructions" (line 313-315) — verbatim into the job summary, which renders markdown and a subset of HTML. A crafted test/build message can therefore forge headings, tables, links or a fake "paged for infra reasons, just rerun" narrative on the run page a maintainer reads to decide what to do. The same change treats the same class of data correctly elsewhere: `guard-verdict.mjs:96-98` deliberately wraps page `detail` in a ```text fence with inner fences defanged, precisely "so crafted markdown/HTML cannot render as structure on the run page". Apply the identical fencing here.

samples.summary: Fixed `HARNESS_EOF` heredoc delimiter around attacker-influenceable CI output permits $GITHUB_OUTPUT injection
samples.evidence: The refactored step assigns `DIAG="$(node ./scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs)"` and writes it between literal `summary<<HARNESS_EOF` / `HARNESS_EOF` lines (agent-iterate-ci.yml:270-274). The diagnosis text is derived from branch-produced build/test output, so a line consisting exactly of `HARNESS_EOF` terminates the value early and every following line is parsed by the runner as an `key=value` output declaration for this step — arbitrary control of `steps.diag.outputs.*`, which then flows into the fixer's prompt (line 318). Impact is bounded (it cannot set another step's outputs, e.g. the guard's `proceed`), and the delimiter predates this diff, but these are the lines the change rewrites: use a random per-run delimiter (`EOF_$(openssl rand -hex 8)`) or refuse to emit when the payload contains the delimiter.

verdict.reason: The literal observation is correct — loop-status.mjs:259 interpolates `note` with only newline-flattening and a 600-char slice, and no `<!--` defanging exists anywhere in the repo. But the security condition it depends on (an untrusted string reaching `note`) is not present. I enumerated every invocation of the script repo-wide: agent-review-panel.yml:1008-1016, :1279-1284, :1998; agent-fix.yml:538; agent-rerun.yml:236; agent-iterate-ci.yml:236 and :435-440 all pass shell string literals (the one computed piece being a 9-char git SHA). The only non-literal note is `$VERDICT` (agent-review-panel.yml:1439/1448), produced by guardVerdictLine/buildLine (guard-verdict.mjs:34-63), which composes exclusively from the fixed PAGE_REASONS table, the `reason` tag, n()-coerced numbers, stall.reason (one of three fixed strings, rounds.mjs:443/472) and an ISO timestamp (rounds.mjs:110-116). All five page() call sites pass literal reason tags (review-round-guard.mjs:140, 147, 246, 266, 275; default :89). The diff-derived `detail` (review-round-guard.mjs:245/259, attached at :101) is consumed only by renderGuardSummary, where it is already truncated and fence-defanged inside a ```text block written to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (guard-verdict.mjs:91-92) — it never reaches $GITHUB_OUTPUT or --note. Other body surfaces are equally closed: lens names come from the trusted manifest set (loop-status.mjs:148-152), SHAs are sliced to 9 chars (:284/286), checks render as keyed emoji (:166), and ledger records are reduced to numbers behind an author gate (:191-202, :400-405). The described exploit therefore requires a future code change that does not exist; as written this is a defense-in-depth hardening suggestion (minor/nit under this lens), not a present or exploitable vulnerability.
